# Human check (cms-api)

<!-- module-flows:start (generated by .claude/bin/module-index; do not edit) -->

Flows: [`owner-setup`](../../flows/owner-setup/FLOW.md), [`password`](../../flows/password/FLOW.md), [`reviewer`](../../flows/reviewer/FLOW.md), [`sign-in`](../../flows/sign-in/FLOW.md).

<!-- module-flows:end -->

## Purpose

Owns "did a person pass the check for this form" (D25, ADR 0027). cms-api is the only verifier: it holds `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`, calls Cloudflare siteverify and refuses with `400 HUMAN_CHECK_FAILED` or `503 HUMAN_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` (fail closed). Routes opt in with `@RequireHumanCheck(<form id>)`; `reviewer` takes the verifier (`TURNSTILE_VERIFIER`) from here, and `identity` puts the decorator on its six public auth routes (HC-3). Depends on `platform` only.

## Techniques

Layers `domain/application/adapters/http`. The outcome rules are pure (`judgeSiteverifyAnswer`: action compared only when one is expected, hostname must be in the expected list when it is not empty, `internal-error` is unavailable). `TurnstileClient` skips the action comparison only with Cloudflare's always-pass test secret (`TURNSTILE_ALWAYS_PASS_TEST_SECRET` in `config/Config.constants.ts`, shared with the production config guard). `HumanCheckGuard` reads `turnstileToken` from the parsed JSON body and the form id from route metadata, resolves the client IP with `ClientIpResolver` (D7) and logs a refusal with route and error code only, never the token. It must run after the IP rate-limit rules and before the email-keyed ones (`@ThrottleAccount`, `@RequireHumanCheck`, `@ThrottleIp` from top to bottom, or `@RequireHumanCheck` above `@Throttle` when the policy is IP-only) and before the request schema and any credential or database work.

## Technologies

NestJS guards and `Reflector`; zod (`turnstileTokenSchema`, the siteverify reply); Cloudflare Turnstile siteverify over `fetch` with a 5 s timeout.

## Entry points

No route of its own. `index.ts` exports `HumanCheckModule`, the decorator `RequireHumanCheck(formId)`, `HUMAN_CHECK_FORMS`, `HUMAN_CHECK_ERROR_CODES`, `TURNSTILE_TOKEN_FIELD`, `turnstileTokenSchema`, `withoutTurnstileToken` (drops the token before a use case), `TURNSTILE_VERIFIER` and the `TurnstileVerifier` type. The module exports `HumanCheckService` and `HumanCheckGuard` for the importing module's routes. Config group `humanCheck` (`expectedHostnames`, `isTestSecretAllowed`) from `TURNSTILE_EXPECTED_HOSTNAME` (comma-separated) and `ALLOW_TURNSTILE_TEST_SECRET`; form ids, token field and codes are published in `content/public-constants.json`.

## Where to change what

To protect another form: add the id to `HUMAN_CHECK_FORMS` (and the form-commons kit; the contract tests keep both equal), put `@RequireHumanCheck(<form>)` and `turnstileTokenSchema` on the route. Another provider is a second adapter behind `TurnstileVerifier`. Keep the secret inside `adapters/Turnstile.client.ts` and the token out of logs.
